texts: good. the named site, Sailsworn as the inspector, and the 'once each season' rate are all carried as licensed atoms, and the habitual clause correctly takes no tense marker.

mixed: the sentence parses cleanly on its own, but each sentence is parsed in isolation, so 'the inspection' and 'the pools' mint brand-new symbols with nothing tying them back to Sailsworn or to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools of the previous line. Name the participants: "Sailsworn's inspection checks the Salt-bloom Tide-pools for erosion."

mixed: the parse seals the complement under the confirming event and also asserts the bloom's growth at top level, which is presumably what you want, but only because 'confirm' was read as factive - the instruction set never classifies it, so a re-parse could treat it like 'say' or 'report' and drop the growth claim entirely. Assert the growth in its own clause and point the confirming at it: "The bloom is growing, and Sailsworn's inspection confirms this."

mixed: 'periodically' has no carrier - a recurrence with no stated period fits neither the every-N-units slot nor a rate, so it is silently dropped and the parse says only that the Council begins fresh ledgers. 'fresh' is also a different word from the 'new ledger' the next sentence's rule keys on, so that rule will never fire on this one. State a period and use one adjective: "The Council begins a new ledger every year." - any stated period ('every season', 'every ten years') works the same way.

good. the adjudicator accepted it: 'each new ledger' becomes a fireable per-ledger rule, with the speaker kept as a shared constant and the first page minted per ledger and linked back to it. It keys on ledgers described as 'new', so keep that adjective consistent with the preceding sentence.
good. the multi-word name is one symbol with its Name atom, 'the first page' is ranked first and linked to the ledger, and the dating event carries its agent, its object and past tense.
